facts.big: I’d like · Would you like · Can you…?
facts.label: Pedir e oferecer
facts.sub: Use I’d like para pedir: I’d like some juice, please. Use Would you like para oferecer: Would you like some pie? Use Can you para pedir ajuda: Can you pass the bread?

facts.label: Pedido
facts.sub: Para pedir com educação, use I’d like + coisa: I’d like some apple juice, please. I’d like é a forma curta de I would like. É mais educado que I want.

facts.label: Pedir ajuda
facts.sub: Para pedir que alguém faça algo, use Can you + verbo base: Can you pass the bread? Responda Sure ou Of course. Acrescente please para soar gentil.

pages.title: A long table · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Sunday at one o’clock in a house in Edinburgh. A long table stands in the dining room. Yuki puts a big pot on a mat. Her friend Max comes in with a cake. The room smells of warm bread. Yuki welcomes him.
“Hi, Max! Welcome to our Sunday lunch. What would you like to drink?” says Yuki. “I’d like some apple juice, please.” says Max. “Sure. Would you like some soup first?” says Yuki.
